text:
infra-monitor: ALERT: Prod-canary for runtime-service (v3.2.1) reporting sustained 5xx spike. 5xx rate ~12% over last 2m, latency up. Auto-rollout paused. @oncall please ack.
leo: acked. I see the dashboard — canary is showing errors for requests with long-context. Looks correlated with the new attention kernel.
tamika: paging oncall. tagging @prateek who is scheduled for infra today.
prateek: I'm on it. pulling logs now. any customer-facing pages?
leo: preliminary SLO impact: ~2% of requests across all tenants hit the canary path. But one high-volume tenant sees ~8% errors since 2026-03-15T14:05Z.
prateek: thanks. I'm going to roll the canary back to v3.2.0 unless someone objects. do we have a quick feature-flag kill available?
sarah: there's a feature flag (runtime.kernel_v2) that gates the kernel change, but the flag was scoped to canary only. we can flip the global kill (runtime.kernel_v2_global=false) to force fallback, but that will affect dedicated nodes. recommend rollback first.
leo: agree — manual rollback for the canary. set expectation ~5-10m to complete and verify.
oncall-bot: @prateek is the on-call for infra. Incident created: INC-20260315-234. Priority: P1. Pager duty escalation to follow.
prateek: executing rollback command now:
```
# roll canary back to v3.2.0
redwood deploy rollback --service runtime-service --env prod-canary --to-version v3.2.0 --reason "canary 5xx spike"
```
prateek: command returned job id 98432. rolling pods one-by-one with graceful termination 45s.
ben: doing a quick watch on metrics + logs. Kibana query I'm running: `service:runtime-service AND env:prod-canary AND status:[500 TO 599] AND @timestamp:>=now-10m`
ops-bot: Deploy job 98432 started by prateek. Estimated ETA 6 minutes.
leo: I'll coordinate client routing -- shifting 100% of canary traffic to stable for now. patching the routing rule.
prateek: rollback finished on 3 of 4 canary hosts, final host draining.
ben: errors trending down — 5xx rate down to 3% across canary.
prateek: rollback complete. job 98432 status=success.
sarah: verifying health endpoints and running smoke: `for t in tenantA tenantB; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://api.redwood.example/$t/generate; done`
ben: smoke looks good for tenantA/tenantB, both 200. Kibana shows error count back to baseline.
leo: customer impact: brief degradation window ~14:04-14:18Z. ETA to notify support: I will open a short incident summary and flag any customer tickets for affected tenant.
tamika: creating support ticket bundle. Tentative severity: P2 for the affected tenant (not global outage).
prateek: root cause hypothesis: new attention kernel for long contexts caused an unhandled edge in KV cache leading to OOM for a subset of worker threads -> 500s. reverting kernel resolves. Will capture reduced repro and create a test.
leo: action items: 1) prateek to run deterministic repro on long-context sequences and create a failing unit test (owner: prateek) 2) sarah to add a canary-level rate limiter for long-context requests (owner: sarah) 3) eng-runtime to prepare a patched kernel with extra guardrails (owner: leo) 4) postmortem doc by EOD tomorrow (owner: leo)
prateek: copying logs and dump to the incident doc: /internal/incidents/INC-20260315-234/logs. I'll also attach heap dumps.
ben: any ETA to re-roll with a patched build? we should avoid rolling until we have a fix + canary staging test.
sarah: agree — hold for verification. we can enable the feature flag in staging and run soak tests for 24h.
leo: communication: I'll post a short update in #customer-bulletins and ping the account manager for the affected tenant.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260315-234 acknowledged by prateek at 2026-03-15T14:12:05Z. Status: mitigated (canary rolled back).
prateek: closing the Slack thread for live rollback coordination. please escalate if you see any regression. final note: no automatic global rollback triggered due to policy; we did manual rollback.
leo: thanks everyone. follow-up in incident doc and postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
